doc.title: Josephine Davies interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 14, 2025

title: Audiences: chamber-music listening versus jazz-club applause
summary: She likes attentive, chamber-style concerts but also enjoys showman audiences like the Joshua Redman live album.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: hear often times standards and things they knew. So does your audience respond or behave differently than if they went to a club and someone was playing “All the Things You Are” and we hear, you know, a little applause after everybody’s solo. I’m imagining that your setting is somewhat different than that.

It can be. Yes. I would say, I mean I do a lot of varied work. My favorite kind of concert is really almost a chamber music concert you know, where people are really turning out to listen and there’s an atmosphere and there’s a sort of responsiveness – that kind of setting. And a lot of the time in that sort of setting I get audience members coming up to me at the end saying, “I was really moved” which makes me so happy because I think that’s such a gift to be able to give something to the world which is going to emotionally connect with strangers. I think that’s just incredible. And that’s what I want when I go to see any kind of performance in any of the arts. I want to be changed as a person. And however, it’s not only that. When I go – maybe I’ll go and see something that perhaps is more in the jazz tradition where you can hear such atmosphere in the audience that maybe it is a little bit more, “Well I’m going to applaud this person’s solo because it was fantastic” and it’s more in that tradition of each person in the band is doing something quite outrageously good and the audience is involved on that level. My example I suppose, funny enough I was listening to this yesterday because I’m taking down one of the tunes on this album which is “Spirit of the Moment” which is Joshua Redman’s album – live album at the Vanguard – maybe it’s – I think it’s the Vanguard. And the audience are just incredible, you know whooping and hollering. And he plays this blues lick on something or other, and they just go nuts for it you know because he’s a real showman, much more so than perhaps I am, and of course it’s just an astonishingly good saxophonist, so he’s really got the audience on his side. And I love that as well. So it’s not always that I want that sort of more chamber music environment. But that’s certainly where I perhaps feel most at home so that the band and I can really develop something, open something up. And that sort of music perhaps is more free, is more of the originals and stuff that I do rather than the standards gigs or things like that. So I guess there are two different areas that I really like to play in, and they’re quite different but perhaps it’s all about just being authentic in the moment.
